title: The Spell of Belief Systems
coreMove: Catch a borrowed belief at the moment it shrinks effort before ability is tested.
sourcePressure: The mindset section begins by showing how beliefs act as hidden ceilings on what effort, persistence, and learning methods feel reasonable.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Claiming belief alone removes every real constraint.
sourceAnchorNote: Frozen sidecar contains no chapter-local named figure, named study, named place, or dated anecdote. Use fictional protagonists and keep source alignment at the concept and title-pressure level.

hook: Do not open The Spell of Belief Systems with a generic unlocked potential claim.
Do not start with a definition of the spell of belief systems.
counterintuition: Do not use a not X but Y correction shell.
Do not claim the opposite of common sense in generic coaching language.
tryThisNow: Do not use set a timer and reflect.
Do not ask the reader to journal broadly without a visible action.
examples: No repeated desk, kitchen, classroom, commute, or generic meeting shells.
No six examples built around timestamp plus named protagonist plus decision.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: owner believes she is bad at numbers
exampleSpecs.stakes: a wrong seasonal order can tie up cash for months
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia catches the old belief when it tells her not to open the sales sheet, then tests one column with last year's receipts.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: paperback stacks leaning beside a sales spreadsheet

exampleSpecs.audience: new official told he is too quiet to control games
exampleSpecs.stakes: weekend tournament assignments depend on certification
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Nicolas separates quiet voice from unclear signal and practices the whistle-hand sequence in front of two peers.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a silver whistle resting on a rulebook

exampleSpecs.audience: student convinced she has no artistic eye
exampleSpecs.stakes: kiln space is scarce and test tiles cost money
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Astrid labels the inherited belief, then lines up three glaze tests to see what the clay actually shows.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: test tiles drying on a wire rack

exampleSpecs.stakes: funding for after-school meals depends on the budget narrative
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marco asks which budget term is blocking him and writes one plain translation beside it instead of repeating that he is not a finance person.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a grant budget printed with one red circle

exampleSpecs.audience: deckhand raised on the belief she lacks spatial sense
exampleSpecs.stakes: fog drills decide whether she advances to mate training
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marta pauses before surrendering the chart and plots the buoy sequence one mark at a time.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a grease pencil dot on a laminated harbor chart

exampleSpecs.audience: engineer believes persuasive people are born that way
exampleSpecs.stakes: a product pilot depends on explaining the prototype clearly
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Yusuf records two demo openings, compares where prospects got lost, and treats persuasion as a tested behavior.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: prototype board beside a laptop webcam

tryThisNowSpec: Catch one belief sentence that starts with I am not the kind of person who, then write what evidence would actually test it.
